claims.text: Almost-equiatomic FeCoNi has an FCC structure.
FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt exhibit soft ferromagnetism and low coercivity.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 5–10 at.% W to FeCoNi.
A FeCoNi-W composition containing 5–10 at.% W remains sufficiently near-equiatomic to qualify as a high-entropy alloy.
The proposed FeCoNi-W compositions have configurational entropy of at least 1.0R.
Suitable rapid-solidification or controlled-annealing conditions can preserve a homogeneous FCC FeCoNi-W phase.
W atoms incorporated in the FCC lattice produce local lattice distortion and strain fields.
The W-induced distortion disrupts local symmetry and enhances magnetic anisotropy.
W has a relatively large atomic radius.
W-induced lattice distortions create pinning centers for magnetic domain walls.
Stronger domain-wall pinning and increased magnetocrystalline anisotropy impede domain-wall motion and raise coercivity.
FeCoNi containing 5–10 at.% W will have higher coercivity than FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
The W-modified alloy will maintain high saturation magnetization.
Keeping W content within 5–10 at.% avoids secondary-phase formation and excessive grain-boundary segregation.
Secondary phases or excessive grain-boundary segregation could degrade magnetic performance or disrupt the FCC structure.

contradictions.description: A four-component alloy with only 5–10 at.% W and roughly 30–32 at.% of each host element is not almost equiatomic across all four components under the ordinary meaning of that constraint, although the intervention calls it near-equiatomic.

The stated prediction and baseline use FeCoNiPd/FeCoNiPt as comparators, whereas the experiment and falsification rule compare W-doped material only with undoped FeCoNi. Failure or success against undoped FeCoNi does not directly resolve the claimed comparison with the Pd/Pt derivatives.
